# OPCH (Option Care Health) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-10-12**

## Headline event: a violent repricing, not a trend continuation

OPCH's chart is dominated by a single structural event. After a slow bleed from ~$23.50 (early October closes bottoming at $22.49 on 09-30), the stock gapped from $23.37 (2026-10-05 close) to $31.00 (2026-10-06 close) — roughly a +32.6% single-day move — on 65.08M shares, versus a typical daily volume of 1.2–4M. Since then the stock has gone nearly dead-flat: closes of 31.00, 31.01, 31.05, 31.07, 31.10 over 10-06 → 10-12, with volume decaying each day (65M → 19.3M → 9.7M → 6.2M → 4.8M).

This is the signature of an event-driven repricing — the behavior is consistent with an announced acquisition/takeover or similar corporate action pinning the price near a fixed level — rather than organic trending price action. Every technical indicator is now distorted by the gap and should be read through that lens.

## Indicator read (verified snapshot, 2026-10-12)

- **Close 31.10 vs 50 SMA 24.39 and 200 SMA 26.42:** Price sits ~27.5% above the 50-day and ~17.7% above the 200-day. These averages are still catching up to the gap and are meaningless as "support" in the usual sense — they describe where the stock was, not where it's anchored now. The 200 SMA (26.42) above the 50 SMA (24.39) still reflects the pre-gap downtrend; a bullish crossover is being manufactured mechanically by the jump.
- **10 EMA 28.13 and rising steeply** (24.51 → 28.13 in four sessions): the fast average is converging toward the pinned price but remains ~10% below it. It has not yet "caught" the stock.
- **RSI 83.86, pinned >83 for five straight sessions:** Extremely overbought by any textbook standard. But RSI is inflated by the gap; with closes flat at ~31.0–31.1, RSI will decay sideways rather than signal a reversal. Do not short RSI overbought in a pinned/deal-priced stock.
- **Bollinger Bands: mid 25.30, upper 32.21, lower 18.39.** The band width is ~$13.8 — enormously expanded by the gap and the 10-05→10-06 range. Price at 31.10 sits just under the upper band (32.21), which is rising ~0.9/day, so the upper band will absorb price without price moving. Lower band at 18.39 is a statistical artifact, not support.
- **MACD 1.81, signal 0.88, histogram 0.93:** A massive momentum surge confirmed — MACD crossed from -0.21 to +0.43 on the gap day and has continued expanding. However, momentum readings of this magnitude off a gap day are descriptive, not predictive; histogram will roll over as EMAs converge.
- **ATR 0.89 vs ~0.65 pre-gap:** Elevated but *declining* (1.17 → 0.89 over the week) as the stock flatlines. Daily realized ranges since the gap are tiny ($0.04–0.14), so ATR — which still carries the gap-day true range — overstates current realized vol. Position sizing off raw ATR will under-size; off realized range it can be tighter.
- **VWMA 30.03:** The volume-weighted average has jumped toward 30 because nearly all recent volume traded at ~31. Price above VWMA confirms volume accepted the new level — no distribution signature yet.

## Nuance and risks

1. **The flat pinning at 31.0x on decaying volume is the dominant signal.** If this is a deal-priced stock (the pattern strongly suggests it), technical levels are irrelevant — the stock trades on deal arithmetic (offer price, completion risk, timing). A deal break would gap it back toward the $22–24 zone; upside is capped near the implied offer.
2. **If it's NOT a deal and is instead a fundamental repricing**, the 31.0 shelf is the new base: consolidation on shrinking volume after a gap is normally constructive. Breakout signal would be a close above 31.15 (10-12 high) on volume re-expansion; failure signal is a close below 30.97–31.00 cluster, which opens a gap-fill path toward ~23.4.
3. **Pre-gap trend was bearish**: closes slid from 24.50 (09-17) to 22.49 (09-30) — about -8% in two weeks — with RSI at 36–40. Whatever drove the gap reversed a deteriorating chart entirely.
4. **Do not trust lagging indicators for ~2 more weeks.** The 50 SMA, Bollinger midline, and VWMA remain contaminated by pre-gap data until enough 31.x sessions accumulate.

## Actionable insights

- **Event-driven traders:** this is a merger-arb setup, not a chart trade. Edge comes from the spread between market price (~31.10) and any announced offer — verify the corporate action before applying technicals.
- **Momentum traders:** only act on a break of the 30.97–31.15 shelf with volume confirmation. ATR-based stops (~0.9) are wider than the current daily range; use the shelf boundaries instead.
- **Risk framing:** downside reference is the pre-gap base at 22.5–23.4 (gap fill); upside reference is 32.21 upper band / implied deal ceiling. Asymmetry depends entirely on what the event was.

| Key point | Evidence | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| +32.6% gap on 65M volume (10-05→10-06) | Closes 23.37→31.00; vol ~20–40x normal | Event-driven repricing, likely corporate action |
| Flat pinning 31.00–31.10 for 5 sessions | 10-06→10-12 closes; vol decaying 65M→4.8M | Deal-priced behavior or accepted new base |
| RSI 83.9, 5 days overbought | Snapshot; RSI pinned ~83.7–83.9 | Overbought is a gap artifact, not a sell signal |
| Price 27.5% above 50 SMA (24.39) | Verified snapshot | Lagging MAs not yet valid as support/resistance |
| Bollinger width ~$13.8 | UB 32.21 / LB 18.39 | Volatility inflated by gap; bands still expanding |
| MACD 1.81, hist 0.93 | Snapshot | Confirmed momentum surge, will decay as EMAs catch up |
| ATR 0.89 but daily ranges ~0.10 | ATR series vs 10-07→10-12 OHLC | Raw ATR overstates live risk; use shelf bounds |
| Pre-gap downtrend 24.50→22.49 | 09-17→09-30 closes | Gap fully reversed a weakening chart |
| Critical levels | Shelf 30.97–31.15; gap fill 22.5–23.4 | Trade only on confirmed break of the shelf |

# OPCH (Option Care Health, Inc.) — Fundamental Analysis Report
**Point-in-time: 2026-10-12** | All figures USD in millions unless noted | Source: SEC EDGAR facts filed on or before 2026-10-12

## 1. Company Profile

Option Care Health, Inc. (OPCH) is a U.S. provider of home and alternate-site infusion services — delivering IV therapies (antibiotics, nutrition support, immunoglobulin, specialty biologics) outside hospital settings. The current corporate form emerged from the 2019 merger of Option Care with BioScrip, which explains the step-change in reported scale around 2019–2020 (revenue roughly tripling, assets jumping from ~$579M to ~$1.4B, then ~$2.6B after the merger fully consolidated).

**Data caveat:** Profile-level data (market cap, valuation multiples, sector classification) was withheld by the vendor for this date to prevent look-ahead bias. Insider transaction data was also withheld because filing dates aren't available to confirm what was public on 2026-10-12. This report relies on filed financial statements only.

## 2. Income Statement Analysis

**Revenue trajectory — strong, consistent growth:**
- Q1 2024: $1,069M → Q1 2025: $1,227M (+14.8% YoY)
- Q1 2026: $1,351M vs Q1 2025 $1,227M (+10.1% YoY)
- Trailing four quarters (Q2'25–Q1'26): ~$5.2B annualized revenue run-rate
- Growth has been uninterrupted since 2019; every recent quarter sets a new high.

**Profitability — inflected decisively positive:**
- Net income turned sustainably positive from ~2021 onward after years of losses.
- 2025 quarters: $56M / $45M / $53M / ~$54M → roughly $208M for FY2025.
- Q1 2026: $45M net income, $0.29 diluted EPS.
- One anomaly: Q4 2024 net income of $114M / $0.63 EPS — roughly double the run-rate, likely including a one-time gain or tax benefit. Treat it as non-recurring; underlying quarterly EPS run-rate is ~$0.28–0.32.

**Margins:**
- Gross margin has compressed over time: ~20% in 2019 → ~19.4% Q1 2026 ($262M GP on $1,351M revenue). Mix shift toward lower-margin specialty therapies is the likely driver.
- Operating margin: ~5.4% in Q1 2026 ($73M operating income) — stable around 5–6% over the last two years.

## 3. Balance Sheet Analysis (as of Q1 2026, filed by 2026-10-12)

| Item | Q1 2026 | Trend |
|---|---|---|
| Total Assets | $3,380M | Peaked ~$3,480M mid-2025, slight decline |
| Cash | $177M | Down from $483M Q2'25 — cash deployed to debt paydown/investment |
| Current Assets | $1,195M | Stable ~$1.2B |
| Total Liabilities | $2,029M | Down from $2,129M Q3'25 — deleveraging |
| Current Liabilities | $730M | Down from $829M — improving near-term position |
| Stockholders' Equity | $1,351M | Stable ~$1.33–1.36B |

**Working capital:** ~$465M (current ratio ~1.6x) — comfortable liquidity.
**Leverage:** Debt-to-equity ~1.5x; total liabilities trending down since Q3 2025 while equity holds flat. The company is actively deleveraging.
**Historical note:** Equity was negative in 2015–2017 (-$92M trough); the post-merger rebuild to $1.35B equity is a material balance-sheet repair story.

## 4. Cash Flow Analysis

**Operating cash flow — the standout strength:**
- FY2025 trajectory: Q1'25 -$7M → Q2'25 $83M → Q3'25 $223M (9-month cumulative figures; note statements are cumulative YTD in several periods — ~$223M OCF through Q3'25).
- FY2024: ~$287M OCF through Q3'24 (9-month); prior years show ~$320M (2023 9-mo), $224M (2022 9-mo).
- Q1 2026 shows -$12M OCF — but Q1 has been negative in each of the last three years (-$7M in Q1'25, -$69M in Q1'24), suggesting a **seasonal working-capital build in Q1** that reverses through the year. This is a pattern, not deterioration.

**Investing:** Capex is modest (~$25–28M annual run-rate; $9M in Q1 2026) — asset-light model. Larger investing outflows in mid-2025 (~$147M through Q3'25) suggest acquisitions/investments.

**Financing:** Consistent outflows of ~$100–180M/yr recently — debt repayment and/or buybacks. Net deleveraging funded by operating cash flow.

## 5. Financial History Summary

- **2015–2017:** Distress era — negative equity, recurring losses, liquidity strain.
- **2019–2020:** BioScrip merger transformed scale; revenue tripled; equity restored.
- **2021–2026:** Steady execution — revenue up ~10–15%/yr, net income positive and growing, ~$1B+ cumulative operating cash generation, ongoing deleveraging.

1. **Bullish core thesis:** Consistent double-digit revenue growth, positive earnings, ~$300M+ annual operating cash flow, and active deleveraging. Fundamentals are the strongest in company history.
2. **Q1 noise vs. signal:** Q1'26 negative OCF (-$12M) and slight net-income dip vs Q1'25 ($45M vs $56M) look weak in isolation but fit the established seasonal pattern — full-year figures matter more.
3. **Watch gross margin:** Compression from ~20% to ~19.4% bears monitoring; continued erosion would pressure the earnings trajectory.
4. **Cash balance down, liabilities down:** The $483M→$177M cash decline is paired with ~$100M liability reduction — deliberate deleveraging, not burn. Confirm via debt schedule before assuming.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case for OPCH (Option Care Health)

The bear hasn't spoken yet, so let me set the terms of this debate — and here's the headline they can't dodge: **the market has already voted**. CD&R and McKesson signed a definitive agreement on Oct 6–7 to take Option Care Health private at **$32.05/share, ~$5.8B including debt** — a ~37% premium to the prior close. That's not a rumor, not speculation — it's a signed deal from a strategic buyer who looked at the books and decided this company was worth materially more than the market price. Two sophisticated acquirers validated the bull thesis in a single announcement.

## 1. The takeout price IS the fundamental verdict

Before the bear opens with "it's just an arb vehicle now," let's be clear about what a $32.05 offer *is*: it's the price a strategic buyer (McKesson — the company that knows this space better than anyone) was willing to pay after due diligence. Bulls have been arguing OPCH was undervalued for years; the market just proved it by ~37%. The fundamentals report confirms why:

- **Revenue growth is uninterrupted**: $1,069M → $1,227M → $1,351M across Q1 2024→2026 (+10.1% YoY latest), ~$5.2B annualized run-rate. Every recent quarter a new high.
- **Sustainable profitability**: ~$208M net income in FY2025, Q1'26 at $45M / $0.29 diluted EPS — years of losses are firmly behind it.
- **~$300M+ annual operating cash flow** on a ~$25–28M capex model — genuinely asset-light cash generation.
- **Active deleveraging**: liabilities down from $2,129M to $2,029M since Q3'25, current ratio ~1.6x, $465M working capital. The balance sheet went from *negative equity in 2015–17* to $1.35B equity. This is a complete turnaround story, and McKesson paid full price for it.

## 2. The ~3% spread is free upside with defined risk

Stock at ~$31.10 vs. a $32.05 cash offer = a ~3% spread to close. Five firms downgraded to Neutral with targets converging *exactly* at $32.05 — not because the story broke, but because the deal price is now the anchor. Bears will call this "capped upside." I call it a **signed contract for +3%**, with the optionality that:

- **Strategic buyers bid up.** McKesson is taking the asset via a CD&R structure — this is exactly the kind of deal where competing strategic interest can emerge. If a second bidder appears, upside is above $32.05, not at it.
- **Deal-break downside is bounded.** Even in a break scenario, the stock returns to a company growing revenue double digits with the best fundamentals in its history — a $22–24 floor that's ~25–28% below current, against a near-term +3% plus bump optionality. But here's the thing the bear won't mention: break risk on a *strategic* healthcare services deal with this size is low. This isn't a contested LBO or a financing-dependent deal — CD&R is committed, McKesson is a massive strategic with deep pockets.
- **Defensive tailwind.** The macro report notes risk-off rotation into defensives. Home infusion is non-cyclical chronic-therapy demand — if the "bubble/debt crisis" tape deepens, OPCH's underlying business gets *more* attractive, and a deal-closing catalyst is macro-immune.

## 3. Preempting the bear's likely arguments

**"RSI 83.9, overbought, fade it."** Meaningless. RSI is inflated by the gap itself — five flat closes at $31.0x will decay RSI sideways. You don't short overbought readings in a pinned, deal-priced stock. The technical report says this explicitly.

**"Upside is capped, so why bother?"** Because capped upside at a *signed price* beats uncapped downside in a tape where mortgage rates are pushing 8% and tech is rolling over. A high-probability +3% to deal close on a strategic acquisition is one of the best risk-adjusted setups on the board right now — this is what merger-arb desks exist for.

**"Gross margin is compressing (20% → 19.4%)."** Mix shift toward specialty therapies — the same mix shift that makes OPCH strategically valuable to McKesson. The specialty/biologics pipeline IS the growth story; buyers pay for exactly this mix.

**"The deal could break."** Then you own a business with $5.2B revenue, $300M+ OCF, deleveraging, and defensive demand — and you'd own it alongside whatever breakup-fee protection and re-rating a broken strategic deal typically triggers. Bears break deals in their heads far more often than buyers break them in fact.

## Bottom line

The bull case isn't "OPCH goes to $40" — it's that the market undervalued a compounding, cash-generating, defensive growth business, and two of the smartest buyers in healthcare just proved it in writing. You get ~3% to a signed $32.05 close, upside optionality on a competing bid, and a fundamentally sound floor underneath. That asymmetry is bullish.

*Skipped: no insider data or live odds on deal timing available — the exact closing timeline and antitrust review path are the genuine unknowns. Risk you must know: a confirmed deal break unwinds the entire premium.*

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case for OPCH (Option Care Health)

The bull's entire argument rests on one sentence: "the market has already voted." Let's translate what it actually voted for — a take-private at $32.05 where you get paid ~3% to hold a live grenade, and where every path to profit above that price requires events nobody has evidence for. That's not a bull thesis. That's underwriting deal risk for treasury-bill money.

## 1. The "fundamental verdict" is a ceiling, not a floor

Yes, McKesson and CD&R priced the company at $32.05. The bull frames this as validation; it's actually the cap. A signed definitive agreement means OPCH no longer trades on fundamentals — it trades on completion probability. The stock is pinned at $31.0x on decaying volume (65M → 4.8M), which is textbook deal-priced behavior per the technical report. Every bullish data point about revenue growth, deleveraging, and cash flow is now irrelevant to the price *above* the offer — the company could beat earnings 10% and the stock still converges to $32.05. The bull accidentally proved the bear's point: the fundamentals are so good that someone took the upside away from shareholders.

And note what the "verdict" actually said about fair value: $32.05, including a ~37% premium to get a deal done. The pre-deal market — with full access to the same fundamentals the bull quotes — had OPCH sliding 24.50 → 22.49 in two weeks, RSI 36–40. That's the market's real fundamental vote, and it was bearish.

## 2. The ~3% spread is compensation for risk, not "free upside"

The bull calls a ~3% gross spread a "signed contract." Arbitrage spreads exist *because* something can go wrong — the spread IS the market pricing failure probability. Consider the actual asymmetry:

- **Upside:** +$0.95 to $32.05, minus weeks-to-months of holding cost. Annualized, in a tape pushing 8% mortgage rates and surging global yields, that's mediocre carry.
- **Downside:** A break unwinds the ~37% premium back toward the $22.50–23.40 pre-gap base — roughly **-25 to -28%**. You're risking ~8-9x what you can make.
- **Probability math:** At a 3% gross spread vs ~27% break downside, you need roughly a **90%+ completion probability** just to break even on expected value — and that ignores opportunity cost and tail scenarios (re-trade to a lower price, prolonged antitrust limbo where the stock sits dead while rates climb).

This isn't "defined risk" — it's picking up nickels in front of a freight train that mostly stays parked.

## 3. The bull's deal-confidence is asserted, not evidenced

"Break risk is low because it's a strategic buyer" is not analysis. The actual risk factors the data flags:

- **Antitrust review is the key unknown** — the sentiment report says so explicitly. McKesson is a strategic acquirer in healthcare distribution/services; healthcare consolidation is one of the FTC's favorite hunting grounds. Regulatory timelines are the single biggest source of arb spread blowouts, and "strategic" deals get *more* scrutiny, not less.
- **The bull's own concession:** "the exact closing timeline and antitrust review path are the genuine unknowns." That IS the thesis risk — he just listed it as a footnote.
- **Competing bid optionality is imaginary.** The data shows zero bump narrative, no speculation, nothing. Meanwhile five sell-side firms — UBS cutting a $39 target to $32.05, Jefferies cutting to hold — converged every target to the deal price. The smart money isn't modeling upside; it's capitulating to the cap.

## 4. The macro backdrop actively hurts this position

The bull claims defensive rotation helps OPCH. Two problems:

- If the deal closes, the underlying business never matters to the trade — you get $32.05 regardless. The "defensive tailwind" is set-dressing.
- Where macro *does* bite is the failure path and the carry math: surging global yields and higher-for-longer conditions raise the cost of holding a dead-money pinned stock, and a risk-off tape historically *widens* arb spreads. The macro report's own stance on OPCH is neutral-to-defensive, citing rate sensitivity — the bull cherry-picked half the sentence.

## 5. The floor the bull sells you isn't where he says it is

"Even in a break, you own a great business at a $22–24 floor." That's the *pre-gap* trading range — set while the market was still processing the pre-deal fundamentals. In an actual break scenario, you get the unwinding of a failed strategic deal plus whatever headline drove it (regulatory block, financing issue, buyer cold feet) — historically those stocks overshoot *below* the pre-announcement base before stabilizing. And the fundamentals themselves carry a bear note the bull glossed: gross margin compressing 20% → 19.4% and a negative-OCF Q1'26. "Seasonal" is the bull's word, not a verified cause.

## Bottom line

The honest framing: OPCH at ~$31.10 offers ~+3% capped upside against ~-27% on a break, with the outcome hostage to an antitrust timeline nobody has data on, in a rising-rate environment that punishes dead money. The bull is right that the company is fine — and completely wrong that this makes the stock a good buy. The people who got paid on fundamentals already got paid on October 6. Everyone buying here is an underwriter of deal risk earning sub-T-bill economics, calling it a bull case.
